candidates.question: Four hypothetical trials use current Preview vector search in an enabled Azure SQL Database environment. Each uses TOP (8), ascending distance ordering and otherwise valid inputs and syntax; any present index matches the column and metric. The matrix varies the approximate clause and correctly placed FORCE_ANN_ONLY hint. Which classification follows the documented contract? 'Optimizer choice' permits ANN or kNN; these are predictions, not measured plans.

answerChoices.text: P: forced ANN; Q: exact kNN; R: error; S: optimizer choice.
P: forced ANN; Q: error; R: exact kNN; S: optimizer choice.
P: forced ANN; Q: error; R: error; S: optimizer choice.
P: forced ANN; Q: error; R: error; S: forced ANN.

candidates.explanation: P has both forcing prerequisites. Q lacks WITH APPROXIMATE and R lacks an index, so the forcing hint causes the documented prerequisite errors. S has no forcing hint, leaving strategy selection to the optimizer.
candidates.deepExplanation: FORCE_ANN_ONLY is a control with requirements, not a general request to fall back gracefully. Both a target vector index and TOP WITH APPROXIMATE must be present when that hint is used. Ordinary unforced search can choose or fall back to kNN, but that does not describe Q or R. S can select ANN without being forced to do so. No trial establishes that ANN improves latency or recall.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Q still has the forcing hint. Missing WITH APPROXIMATE is an error under that hint, not the ordinary unforced exact-kNN form.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: R still has the forcing hint. Without an index it cannot meet the required ANN strategy; the unforced no-index fallback does not apply.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.d: S has no FORCE_ANN_ONLY hint. A compatible index and approximate request permit ANN but do not force the optimizer to select it.

candidates.subskill: Choose between using ANN and ENN for vector search
